tool.name: iCount demultiplex
tool.description: split iCLIP reads by experimental barcode and move randomers into read names
tool.command: #set $has_3prime = False #set $mixed = '' #for $b in $barcodes #if str($b.barcode3).strip() #set $has_3prime = True #else #for $c in $barcodes #if str($c.barcode3).strip() and str($c.barcode5) == str($b.barcode5) #set $mixed = str($b.barcode5) #end if #end for #end if #end for #if $reads.is_of_type('fastqsanger.gz') #set $reads_name = 'input.fastq.gz' #else #set $reads_name = 'input.fastq' #end if #if $mixed ## iCount accepts this, but the 5'-only experiment's reads end up in the 3' no-match file echo "5' barcode" '$mixed' "is listed both with and without a 3' barcode. Give every entry with this 5' barcode a 3' barcode." >&2 && exit 1 && #end if ## iCount writes cutadapt temp files under ICOUNT_TMP_ROOT; keep them inside the job directory export ICOUNT_TMP_ROOT="\$PWD/icount_tmp" && mkdir -p demux unassigned && ln -s '$reads' '$reads_name' && iCount-Mini demultiplex '$reads_name' '$adapter' #for $b in $barcodes '$b.barcode5' #end for #if $has_3prime --barcodes3 #for $b in $barcodes #if str($b.barcode3).strip() '$b.barcode3' #else . #end if #end for #end if --mismatches $mismatches --minimum_length $minimum_length --min_adapter_overlap $min_adapter_overlap --out_dir demux && mv demux/demux_nomatch5.fastq.gz '$nomatch' #if $has_3prime ## reads that passed the 5' step but could not be placed by their 3' barcode && mv demux/no_adapter_found_*.fastq.gz demux/demux_*_nomatch.fastq.gz unassigned/ #end if

param.name: reads
param.label: iCLIP reads
param.help: Single-end reads that still carry the experimental barcode, randomer and 3' adapter.

param.name: adapter
param.label: 3' adapter sequence
param.help: Removed from the 3' end of each read with cutadapt after demultiplexing.

validator.message: Use only the letters A, C, G and T

param.name: barcode5
param.label: 5' barcode
param.help: Experimental barcode at the 5' end of the read, with N marking each randomer (UMI) position, e.g. NNNGGTTNN.

validator.message: Use A, C, G, T and N only, with at least one non-N base

param.name: barcode3
param.label: 3' barcode (optional)
param.help: Experimental barcode just before the 3' adapter, with N for randomer positions. Leave empty when this experiment has only a 5' barcode.

validator.message: Use A, C, G, T and N only, with at least one non-N base

param.label: Mismatches tolerated in the 5' barcode
param.help: Counted over the non-randomer positions. 3' barcodes are always matched exactly.

param.label: Minimum read length after barcode removal
param.help: Reads shorter than this once the 5' barcode is cut off are discarded, before adapter trimming. With 3' barcodes the check is repeated after the adapter and 3' barcode are removed.

param.label: Minimum adapter overlap for 3' barcode assignment
param.help: Only used when 3' barcodes are given: a read must show at least this many bases of the adapter before its 3' barcode is trusted. Reads that do not are reported as unassigned.

has_text.text: is listed both with and without a 3' barcode

tool.help:
## What it does
Splits a multiplexed iCLIP (or eCLIP/irCLIP-style) FASTQ file into one file per experiment, using the experimental barcode at the 5' end of each read and, optionally, a second barcode just before the 3' adapter. It uses the `demultiplex` command of [iCount-Mini](https://github.com/ulelab/iCount-Mini), the maintained fork of the iCount iCLIP pipeline from the Ule lab.
For every read assigned to an experiment, the tool:
1. cuts off the barcode, 2. appends the randomer (UMI) bases, i.e. the `N` positions of the barcode, to the read name as `:rbc:<randomer>`, where later PCR-duplicate removal and cross-link counting expect it (with 3' barcodes the 3' randomer comes first, followed by the 5' one), 3. removes the 3' adapter with cutadapt.
## Barcodes
Give one entry per experiment. Write each barcode as it appears in the read, with `N` for every randomer position and A/C/G/T for the experimental part. Classic iCLIP barcodes look like `NNNGGTTNN` (3 + 2 randomer bases around a 4 nt experimental barcode); iCLIP2 uses longer ones such as `NNNNNCTGCNNNN`.
The experiment is chosen by counting matches at the non-`N` positions; reads with more mismatches than allowed against every barcode go to the *no barcode match* output, untrimmed. A read that is equally close to two barcodes goes to the one listed first. To avoid such ties, keep the experimental parts of your barcodes different in at least twice the allowed number of mismatches plus one positions (3 positions for the default of 1 mismatch).
When 3' barcodes are used, each experiment is a pair of 5' and 3' barcodes, and the same 5' barcode may appear in several pairs. 3' barcodes must match exactly, and a read is only placed by its 3' barcode when at least the *minimum adapter overlap* bases of the adapter are found, since shorter reads may never reach the 3' barcode. A 5' barcode must either always or never be paired with a 3' barcode; mixing the two for the same 5' barcode is rejected, because the 5'-only experiment's reads would otherwise be lost.
## Outputs
- **Demultiplexed reads**: a list collection with one gzipped FASTQ per experiment, named after its barcode (`NNNGGTTNN`, or `NNNGGTTNN_NNATCG` for a 5'/3' pair). - **No barcode match**: reads whose 5' end matched no barcode. - **Unassigned by 3' barcode** (only with 3' barcodes): for each 5' barcode that has 3' barcodes, reads in which no adapter was found (`no_adapter_found_<barcode5>`) and reads whose 3' end matched none of its 3' barcodes (`demux_<barcode5>_nomatch`).
## Dropped reads
Some reads appear in no output at all:
- reads shorter than the longest 5' barcode, - reads shorter than the *minimum length* once the 5' barcode is cut off (checked before adapter trimming; this also applies to reads with no barcode match), - with 3' barcodes, reads shorter than the *minimum length* once the adapter and 3' barcode are removed.
Read names are cut at the first space, so Illumina comments such as `1:N:0:ATCACG` are not kept.
